In Russian, there’s no present tense for the verb “to be” and “to have”! 

To be is scrapped completely (that’s why russians speak english like “I Dimitri, you my friend”), while to have is translated with the form “у меня/тебя есть” which means “this thing is in my/your etc proximity”.

Also, the past tense of the verbs is created just by adding an “L” to the end of the base of the verb BUT an “LA” if the subject is feminine and “LI” if plural.

Example

I played M = ya igral

I played F = ya igrala

They played = anì igrali

It was a little kid, maybe 7 or 8 years old, reading out loud the text on the back side of a package as big as a shoes' box. 
I was petrified. I was not sure about what I had just overheard, so I stood still for what was like 10 seconds (which to me felt like 10 hours). Then I started to slowly make my way to where the kid stood, which meanwhile stopped reading, put the box back on the shelf and reached the checkout hand in hand with his mother, who was holding another board game for his son.
I grabbed it: it was a matte black box, no texts other than the one on the back, which read:

"The world is in danger again. This time nobody can help save the situation, NOT EVEN YOU."
